summary: Threading + temp files for IPC is fragile; use st.fragment(run_every=N) for polling
failure_scenario: Temp files in global dir collide under concurrent runs; no cleanup on crash; tempnam race on Windows. st.fragment with run_every auto-refreshes a function on a timer without external files.

summary: Three identical temp-file readers (_read_progress, _read_log, _read_summary) need abstraction
failure_scenario: Adding a fourth temp channel means copying the same try/except pattern again; each has slightly different default-return type (dict, list, None) but identical template logic.

summary: URL parsing uses str.split() instead of urllib.parse for site_cfg in custom URL branch
failure_scenario: URL like 'https://example.com/viec-lam/tag?q={keyword}' with '/viec' substring in query param mis-parses 'base_url'. split('/')[3:] fails on URL with fewer than 3 segments, raising IndexError.

summary: except Exception as exc: pass silently swallows all crawl failures
failure_scenario: If run_all_scrapers raises (network down, config error, memory), thread exits silently; user sees stale progress or empty summary with no error feedback.

summary: use_fallback default changed from True to False, undocumented behavioral change
failure_scenario: Users upgrading silently lose synthetic fallback after crawl; expected data appears absent. No migration warning or config-level default.

summary: crawl_results session state never populated by new threading flow; Tab 2 broken after crawl
failure_scenario: Thread writes summary to temp file but never sets st.session_state.crawl_results. Tab 2 falls through to parquet-recovery (fails if dir empty) or shows 'Run a crawl first' right after a successful crawl.

summary: Log temp file scraper_log.txt cleared but never written to; UI shows empty logs during auto-refresh
failure_scenario: Line 108 truncates scraper_log.txt; _read_log() reads same file. But _run() writes only to local StringIO handler. During auto-refresh polling (lines 86-93), _read_log() always returns empty, so no log lines displayed during crawl.

summary: scraper_crawling.pid written but never read; dead code
failure_scenario: PID file written on start and finish but _crawling state is driven solely by st.session_state.crawling. If session state resets mid-crawl (e.g. stale browser tab), PID file lingers but is never checked. Dead write path with no consumer.
